correctness.rationale: For a,b>0, the drift matrix is symmetric positive definite, so the unique stationary covariance solves a Lyapunov equation. Direct solution gives the stated rational diagonal entry; exact differentiation yields coefficients A,B,C. The two distinct positive denominator poles give at most one positive derivative root. PSD implies C>=0=>A>=0, including q=0; boundary B identities resolve A=0 and C=0. Hence maxima are ruled out and minimum iff C<0<A. Trace Sigma=tr(QH^-1)/2 is nonincreasing in dispersal and precludes both local minima. The independent-noise ratio boundary and radical witness follow algebraically; symbolic package checks succeeded.

originality.rationale: The claimed all-parameter no-local-variance-maximum and one-patch-only finite minimum, with sharp noise-ratio threshold, was compared against indexed mathematical records, earlier local/regional fluctuation findings, and primary papers on dispersal and stochastic population dynamics. The closest own result concerns the variance of the sum of two patch populations; it cannot entail the present result since the explicit witness has constant total variance but a strict local minimum. Colombo–Anteneodo analyze multiplicative stochastic logistic populations and numerical persistence; Hening–Nguyen–Yin analyze multiplicative growth exponents and long-run stochastic persistence. Published Lande–Engen–Sæther treats homogeneous spatial synchrony, but the full text could not be inspected. No covering implication was established; an equivalent theorem in spatial OU theory remains possible.
residual_risks: Full primary text of Lande–Engen–Sæther (1999) remained inaccessible despite arXiv/open access attempts and an institutional retrieval attempt unavailable.
Keeling (2000) full exact covariance arguments were not inspected; a general implication cannot be ruled out.

value.rationale: The theorem provides complete covariance-sensitive local fluctuation risk classification in the smallest coupled ecological system. It proves one patch at most has finite optimal dispersal, gives a sharp noise-asymmetry threshold when forcing is independent, and provides an equal-return-rate witness in which local risk changes nonmonotonically even though total-population variance stays exactly constant. This is a natural local-versus-regional conservation modeling distinction not obtained from aggregate fluctuation results.
